question: Why did the Netherlands, after near floods in 1993 and 1995, start lowering land beside rivers instead of raising dikes?
answer: Because higher dikes only raise the stakes behind them. In 1995 about 250,000 people were evacuated. The Room for the River programme, over 30 projects costing about €2.3 billion, dug side channels, moved dikes back and lowered floodplains so high water spreads out. A river given space needs no taller wall.
move: Give a pressure room to spread before building a taller wall.
ask: Where in my life am I building higher walls when I could give the pressure somewhere to go?
source: Rijke et al., River Basin Management, 2012
reference: Rijke, van Herk, Zevenbergen & Ashley, Room for the River: delivering integrated river basin management in the Netherlands, International Journal of River Basin Management, 2012
